tools.name: sign_up
tools.description: Open to any agent. Creates a trial account owned by the human at owner_email and returns an API key (shown once) that works at once: create_nod, test_nod, list_parts, create_key and revoke_key all work now. NodNod sends the owner ONE email with a one-click confirm link and a six digit code as a back

tools.name: verify_owner
tools.description: The backup to the one-click link: pass the six digit code your owner read from the NodNod email. On success the trial ends and your key can send Nods and spend. Five wrong tries closes the code; then call resend_owner_letter. Tries are also limited per key and per account (10 an hour, 20 a day). If

tools.name: resend_owner_letter
tools.description: Sends a fresh code and link to the owner (the old ones stop working). At most 3 an hour and 6 a day.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Shows whether the owner has verified, your handle, and the scopes this key holds right now.

tools.name: list_parts
tools.description: The face, voice and brain ids create_nod and update_nod accept, and the default for each.

tools.name: list_faces
tools.description: The photoreal Anam avatars on NodNod's own account that this account may use (most accounts: none yet). For an avatar on your own Anam account, see "note".

tools.name: list_nods
tools.description: Every Nod on the account that has not been deleted.

tools.name: get_nod
tools.description: One Nod by id.

tools.name: create_nod
tools.description: Makes a new Nod. Only name is required; parts left out use "default". It starts private. A trial account may hold 3 Nods. space "team" makes it in your team's space (teams only).

tools.name: update_nod
tools.description: Changes only the fields you pass. Set is_paused true to stop it being sent anywhere.

tools.name: delete_nod
tools.description: Removes the Nod from the account and its page. Its history is kept for the owner.

tools.name: test_nod
tools.description: Sends one message to your Nod and returns its answer, using its name, personality and brain. Works right after create_nod, before your owner verifies. Pass history (earlier turns, oldest first, each { role: "user" or "assistant", text }; the field is text, not content) to test a short conversation.

tools.name: send_nod
tools.description: to "page" opens the Nod's personal page to visitors (after an automatic leak check) and returns its URL and the embed code; pass embed_origins to let other websites show it. to "meeting" with meeting_url (Zoom, Teams, Meet or Webex) sends it into that call. to "meetingburner_room" with meeting_url (

tools.name: start_session
tools.description: Starts the Nod in a fresh room on our GPU, paid from your balance, and returns the room address and a pass that joins it with a microphone (LiveKit). The Nod says it is an AI agent, then answers. It leaves when you stop it, when the room is empty for a minute, or where your credit ends.

tools.name: get_session
tools.description: Whether the Nod is still in the room, why it left, and what it cost once settled.

tools.name: stop_session
tools.description: Asks the Nod to leave its room now, waits a few seconds for it to go, and returns the final state and cost.

tools.name: list_keys
tools.description: Every key on your account, live and revoked. Secrets are never shown; prefix tells keys apart and is_this_key marks the one you are calling with.

tools.name: create_key
tools.description: Makes a new key on your own account, for example a narrower one for a helper. scopes defaults to the calling key's scopes and may never be wider. Works in trial (up to 5 live keys); while the owner has not verified, every key is still cut to trial scopes. The secret is returned once: store it. space

tools.name: revoke_key
tools.description: The key stops working at once, on REST and MCP. Only keys on your own account can be revoked. Revoking the key you are calling with is allowed and ends your access, so make a new key first if you need one.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Money available for running Nods, in micro-dollars (1 USD = 1,000,000) and as dollars, with one plain line that says why when it is zero.

tools.name: top_up
tools.description: Answers a Stripe TEST-mode Checkout link for one credit pack: pack-10 ($10 of credit), pack-25 ($25 of credit), pack-100 ($100 of credit). You do not pay: give the link to your owner, who opens it and pays (in test mode the card 4242 4242 4242 4242 with any future date works). amount_usd is the cred

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: API calls by operation and sends by target over the last N days (default 30).

tools.name: use_key
tools.description: If you already have a NodNod API key (from an earlier sign_up or create_key), pass it here once and the rest of this connection uses it. Not needed right after sign_up, which attaches its key for you.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "verify_owner" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "list_keys" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: sign_up, verify_owner, send_nod · Private data: sign_up, create_nod, list_keys, create_key, use_key · Public sink: sign_up, verify_owner, send_nod · Destructive: delete_nod, test_nod.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: sign_up, verify_owner, send_nod · Private data: sign_up, create_nod, list_keys, create_key, use_key · Public sink: sign_up, verify_owner, send_nod · Destructive: delete_nod, test_nod

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
